sources.population: Mild idiopathic CTS,13 men/67 women among completers
sources.comparator: Splint plus median-nerve/tendon glides versus splint alone
sources.coInterventions: Night splint, daytime as needed in both arms
sources.outcomes: No between-group symptom/function/grip/pinch advantage; within-group gains cannot prove added benefit.
sources.uncertainty: Repeated fulltext challenges; AAOS appendix gives3×daily,10reps,5second holds, but secondary dose not accepted as verified primary protocol.
sources.limitations: 80 mild idiopathic CTS patients completed splint+median nerve/tendon glides versus splint alone over 6 weeks. Splints at night, daytime as needed. No significant between-group difference in symptom/function scores, grip or pinch; within-group improvement cannot establish added glide benefit. AAOS evidence appendix reports exercise 3 times/day, 10 repetitions, each position held 5 seconds; dose is secondary extraction, not independently verified methods. Harms not established by the accessible abstract. This is a limited glide candidate, not default treatment for severe CTS, another nerve diagnosis, or postoperative CTS.

sources.population: 124 volunteers with mild to moderate CTS; narrower analyzed-population details come from cts-g3.
sources.coInterventions: All four groups received nocturnal orthoses plus stretching; no stretch-only, orthosis-only or untreated comparison.
sources.outcomes: Primary abstract: significant time effects at four, twelve and twenty-four weeks; CTQ-Function/DASH interaction at twelve weeks, with post hoc differences for lumbrical-splint/general-stretch and cock-up-splint/lumbrical-stretch combinations versus the other two groups. At twenty-four weeks, a significantly greater percentage with cock-up splint plus lumbrical-intensive stretch achieved clinically important CTQ-Function improvement. Surgery elected by 25.5% by twenty-four weeks. Exact effect sizes, p-values and responder denominators are not supplied in the abstract.
sources.followUp: Assessments at four, twelve and twenty-four weeks; four-week intervention is distinct from follow-up.
sources.uncertainty: Primary abstract supports a frequency and endpoint-specific functional-response advantage, not complete methods or isolated stretch efficacy. The 2019 CPG cts-g3 describes twelve-week differences but concludes no combination superior; endpoint/account discrepancy remains explicitly unresolved.
sources.harms: Primary abstract does not report harms. The 2019 guideline separately says no adverse effects reported; primary ascertainment unknown.
sources.limitations: Full primary methods unavailable. Six-times-daily stretching is explicit, while exact geometry, repetitions, hold, load, progression and stopping rules remain unknown. Preserve the primary twenty-four-week responder advantage alongside the secondary guideline no-superiority summary; do not invent numerical significance/effect size or isolate stretching benefit.

sources.title: Correlation of Segmental Carpal Tunnel Pressures with Changes in Hand and Wrist Positions in Patients with Carpal Tunnel Syndrome and Controls
sources.publicationStatus: Final primary study, Journal of Hand Surgery European Volume 1998;23(5):598–602.

access.details: Primary abstract and/or indexed source passages inspected; complete article inspection not established. [Primary abstract](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1016/S0266-7681%2898%2980009-0). DOI 10.1016/S0266-7681(98)80009-0. 39 CTS patients/12 controls; measured pressure at 1-cm intervals in relaxed/gripping hands across neutral/flexed/extended wrists. Patient pressures exceeded controls; relaxed neutral generally lower, extension often higher than flexion. Position, grip and measurement location interacted; simple universal pressure rules are inappropriate. Mechanistic study, no workout intervention, clinical follow-up or safe angle/load endpoint. Supports exploring a symptom-tolerable wrist position, not declaring all loaded wrist extension harmful. sources.outcomes: 2019 CPG secondary Baker extraction: 103 analyzed, normal two-point discrimination/no thenar atrophy. It describes twelve-week differences and no three-way interaction at four/twenty-four weeks, then summarizes no superior intervention; 25.5% surgery by twenty-four weeks without group difference. Primary abstract cts-p2 instead reports a twenty-four-week clinically important functional-response advantage for cock-up splint plus lumbrical-intensive stretches. Different endpoint/account summaries remain unresolved.
sources.uncertainty: Secondary guideline summary conflicts with the primary abstract on overall superiority interpretation. Do not erase the primary endpoint-specific response or infer isolated stretching efficacy.
sources.harms: Guideline states no adverse effects reported in the Baker trial; full primary harm ascertainment not independently verified.
sources.limitations: Secondary extraction independently re-read at CPG50. No control arm isolates stretching. Exact stretch holds/range/progression remain unknown; orthosis joint angles are not stretch geometry.
